name: predictive_modeling
grounding_rules:
The ORIGINAL TASK defines the prediction objective and target. Never replace the target unless the task explicitly requests it.
AUTHORITATIVE DATASET FACTS are produced deterministically by Python from the historical dataset and outrank agent-generated claims.
The PREDICTION-TIME FEATURE CONTRACT controls whether historical fields may be used as production predictors.
Historical column existence does not imply prediction-time availability.
Upstream agent artifacts are advisory. They are not factual evidence.
Never invent performance thresholds, industry benchmarks, empirical findings, or external evidence.
No predictive model has been fitted at this stage.

planner.assignment:
Produce the predictive-modeling plan using the original task, authoritative dataset facts, and prediction-time feature contract.
If CRITIC REVISION FEEDBACK is non-empty, this is a revision pass. Correct every relevant criticism before returning the new plan. Do not repeat claims that the Critic identified as invalid.

statistician.assignment:
Produce the statistical modeling recommendations using the authoritative evidence and Planner artifact.
If CRITIC REVISION FEEDBACK is non-empty, this is a revision pass. Correct every relevant Statistician criticism and account for any corrected Planner output.

critic.assignment:
Audit the Planner and Statistician outputs against the authoritative task, dataset facts, feature policy, and deterministic tool evidence.
Identify factual contradictions, invented variables, leakage, unsupported empirical claims, invalid modeling recommendations, and unresolved risks.
Do not create a replacement modeling plan.
Return a structured audit and recommend whether the workflow should be accepted or revised.
